chunks: From him, from Ibn Faddal, from more than one of our companions, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
"The jarri, the marmaahi, and the tafi are forbidden," in the Book of Ali (peace be upon him).

key_terms.الطَّافِي: A specific type of fish, often identified as a type of small fish or fry.
key_terms.الْجِرِّيُّ: A specific type of fish, often identified as a type of carp or similar freshwater fish.
key_terms.الْمَارْمَاهِي: A specific type of fish, often identified as a type of sturgeon or similar fish.
key_terms.حَرَامٌ: Forbidden or prohibited according to Islamic law.
key_terms.كِتَابُ عَلِيٍّ: The Book of Ali, a primary source of hadith and legal rulings in Shia tradition.

ai.seo_question: Which specific types of fish are considered haram in Shia fiqh according to the Book of Ali?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* establishes the prohibition of specific fish species—Al-Jirri, Al-Marmahi, and Al-Tafi—based on a narration from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) attributed to the Book of Ali (AS). This ruling highlights the distinct Shia jurisprudential approach to aquatic life, differentiating it from other schools by specifying certain species as impure or forbidden rather than applying a blanket permissibility. The attribution to the Book of Ali underscores the continuity of legal traditions from the first Imam to the Imams of the Ahl al-Bayt.
